**Indikator 7b** is a result indicator managed by the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-DATABASEN]] that measures the proportion of young people in the [[adhd-behandlingspopulation|ADHD-behandlingspopulation]] (ADHD treatment population) who have passed the Danish public school leaving examination (*folkeskolens afgangseksamen*) before turning 17 years old [^src2] [^src4]. It serves as a comparative benchmark to Indikator 7a, allowing evaluators to assess the impact of treatment on educational outcomes by comparing the treatment population with the broader assessment population and the general background population [^src4]. The indicator relies on data from [[danmarks-statistik|Danmarks Statistik]] to track these educational milestones [^src4].

The performance of Indikator 7b highlights a persistent, structural educational lag for young people with ADHD, underscoring the need for targeted support within both the school system and treatment pathways [^src4]. In 2023, the proportion of youth in the ADHD treatment population who passed the exam before age 17 was 65% [^src2]. However, more recent data from the period of April 1, 2024, to March 31, 2025, shows a decline, with Indikator 7b reaching 58% (95% CI: 55–60), down from 67% in the 2022/23 period [^src3]. These findings are part of a broader national quality monitoring effort that has revealed systemic challenges in ADHD care, including significant regional variations in both medical treatment practices and educational outcomes [^src2] [^src4].

The tracking of this indicator follows specific chronological reporting periods. For the 2023/24 annual report, the assessment period for Indikator 7b began on April 1, 2023, and concluded on March 31, 2024 [^src3]. Additionally, the 2024 reporting cycle included an assessment of Indikator 7b for young people who turned 17 in 2024 [^src4]. As the ADHD-DATABASEN's steering committee evaluates the future role of these indicators, the data from Indikator 7b remains crucial for understanding the long-term socioeconomic and educational impacts of ADHD interventions in the Danish healthcare system [^src3] [^src4].
